record.paper_title: Control of multi-agent systems: Results, open problems, and applications
record.context_brief: Control under mean-field, graph-limit, and embedding limits
record.original_question: Consider the heterogeneous N-agent system xi_dot_i = (1/N) sum_j G(t, x_i, x_j, xi_i, xi_j), where x_i is a parameter of agent i that is constant in time, x_dot_i = 0, and xi_i is the state of agent i. This model allows the interaction function G to depend on the specific particle, avoiding the usual indistinguishability assumption of mean-field theory. The system can be related to particle or microscopic descriptions, Liouville probabilistic equations, Vlasov mesoscopic mean-field equations, Euler macroscopic graph-limit equations, graphon or cut-norm limits, and embedding descriptions. For controlled versions of this system, how do control problems behave under these limiting procedures, and can controls be formulated so that the limits give meaningful controlled dynamics across scales?

evidence.quote: control problems behave with respect to such limits

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous system of N interacting agents. Each agent i ∈ {1,...,N} is characterized by a time-invariant parameter x_i ∈ ℝ^d (so dx_i/dt = 0) and a time-dependent state ξ_i(t) ∈ ℝ^k whose evolution is governed by

  dξ_i/dt = (1/N) Σ_{j=1}^{N} G(t, x_i, x_j, ξ_i, ξ_j),  i = 1,...,N,

where G : ℝ_+ × ℝ^d × ℝ^d × ℝ^k × ℝ^k → ℝ^k is a sufficiently regular interaction kernel that may depend on the individual agent labels through (x_i, x_j), thereby relaxing the usual indistinguishability hypothesis of classical mean-field theory.

Introduce a controlled version of this system by adding a control term, e.g.
  dξ_i/dt = (1/N) Σ_{j=1}^{N} G(t, x_i, x_j, ξ_i, ξ_j) + u_i(t),
or, more generally, a control acting on the interaction kernel and/or on each agent, subject to admissibility constraints and a cost functional J_N(u).

As N → ∞, the uncontrolled dynamics admit several limiting descriptions:
 (i) a particle/microscopic ODE description;
 (ii) a Liouville (probabilistic) equation on the empirical measure;
 (iii) a Vlasov-type mesoscopic mean-field PDE for a density f(t, x, ξ);
 (iv) an Eulerian macroscopic graph-limit equation indexed by the parameter x;
 (v) a graphon / cut-norm limit, where the pairwise weights are encoded by a measurable kernel W : [0,1]^2 → ℝ;
 (vi) embedding descriptions that realize all of the above in a common functional-analytic framework.

Problem. Develop a rigorous theory of optimal control for the heterogeneous N-agent system above that is compatible with each of the limits (i)–(vi). Specifically:

(a) Define classes of admissible controls u_i (and corresponding cost functionals) at the N-agent level that admit well-posed limiting notions of control in each of the descriptions (i)–(vi), so that the controlled limit dynamics are themselves meaningful controlled evolutions (e.g., controlled Liouville, controlled Vlasov, controlled graph-limit, controlled graphon equations).

(b) Prove convergence (in an appropriate sense, including Γ-convergence of cost functionals and convergence of value functions or of optimal controls) of the N-agent control problems to the corresponding limit control problems as N → ∞, including under simultaneous graph-limit and mean-field scalings.

(c) Establish commutation (or characterize obstructions to commutation) between the limit N → ∞ and the control synthesis, both in open-loop and feedback formulations, and identify regimes in which the limits (i)–(vi) yield equivalent controlled descriptions via the embedding viewpoint.
artifact.category_tag: Multi-agent control and mean-field / graphon limits
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the behavior of control problems for heterogeneous multi-agent systems under particle, Liouville, Vlasov mean-field, graph-limit, graphon/cut-norm, and embedding limits. Recent literature (graphon mean-field control, graphon mean-field games, mean-field limits of non-exchangeable systems, sparse-graph mean-field control) provides partial results in specific limiting regimes, but a unified theory connecting all of these limits with controlled dynamics and convergence of optimal controls/value functions remains largely open and is an active research direction.

status_evidence.title: Mean-field limit of non-exchangeable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes mean-field limits for non-exchangeable interacting particle systems via graphon-type kernels, without control.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on uncontrolled non-exchangeable mean-field limits, leaving controlled versions across multiple limits open.

status_evidence.title: Graphon Mean Field Games and Their Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Formulates graphon mean field games on infinite networks.
status_evidence.claim: Graphon control/game theory exists but does not unify all limits (i)–(vi).

status_evidence.title: Mean-Field Control on Sparse Graphs: From Local Limits to GNNs via Neighborhood Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Extends mean-field control to sparse-graph local limits.
status_evidence.claim: Active extensions to alternative graph limits suggest the unified problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Probabilistic Analysis of Graphon Mean Field Control
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) analysis of graphon mean field control problems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity indicates the unified control-under-limits problem remains under investigation.
